name: Virginity Claim (Taanat Betulim)
notes: Husband's claim that bride was not a virgin; procedures, burden of proof, credibility of parties

name: Hinnuma (Bridal Veil/Wedding Customs as Evidence)
notes: Use of bridal veil and uncovered hair as evidence of virgin status at time of marriage

name: Ketubah Stipulations (Tena'ei Ketubah)
notes: Court-mandated and voluntary stipulations included in or implied by the ketubah, including redemption from captivity, medical care, daughters' sustenance, widow's residence

name: Widow's Sustenance from Estate (Mezonot Almanah)
notes: A widow's right to be sustained from her late husband's estate until she remarries or collects her ketubah

name: Widow's Right of Residence (Dirat Almanah)
notes: A widow's right to continue residing in her late husband's house; differences between Jerusalem, Galilee, and Judea customs

name: Daughters' Sustenance Stipulation (Mezonot Banot)
notes: Court stipulation that daughters are sustained from the father's estate after his death until married

name: Sons Inheriting Mother's Ketubah (Ketubot Benin Dichrin)
notes: Stipulation that male children of a wife inherit her ketubah amount in addition to their share with other brothers

name: Oath Required for Ketubah Collection (Shevu'at Ketubah)
notes: Circumstances requiring a woman to take an oath before collecting her ketubah, including partial admission, single witness, collection from orphans or liened property

name: Widow's Collection of Ketubah (Gviyat Ketubah)
notes: Procedures and time limits for a widow or divorcée to collect her ketubah, including selling husband's property outside court

name: Ketubah Precedence Among Multiple Wives
notes: Order of collection when a man had multiple wives with competing ketubah claims against the estate

name: Ailonit (Sexually Underdeveloped Woman)
notes: Halakhic status and marriage rights of an ailonit; whether she is entitled to a ketubah

name: Husband Who Rebels Against Wife (Mored)
notes: Incremental increase in ketubah obligation when husband withholds conjugal rights or refuses to support wife

name: Husband's Vow Restricting Wife
notes: Cases where husband vows to restrict wife from food, adornment, visiting family, or attending social gatherings, requiring divorce with ketubah payment

name: Blemishes Discovered After Marriage (Mumim b'Nisuin)
notes: Physical defects discovered after betrothal or marriage; who bears burden of proof and grounds for divorce without ketubah payment

name: Wife's Property Rights During Marriage (Nichsei Melog and Tzon Barzel)
notes: Distinctions between usufruct property (melog) and guaranteed-value property (tzon barzel); husband's rights to produce vs. wife's principal

name: Wife's Work Obligations to Husband
notes: Fixed list of household tasks a wife must perform; how the number of maidservants she brings reduces her obligations

name: Conjugal Frequency Obligation (Onah)
notes: Detailed schedule of conjugal obligations according to husband's occupation (men of leisure, laborers, donkey drivers, camel drivers, sailors)

name: Dowry Assessment and Valuation
notes: Rules for how goods and money of a dowry are assessed in the ketubah; the one-fifth inflation of goods valuation

name: Obligation to Sustain Stepdaughter
notes: A husband who stipulates to sustain his wife's daughter from a prior relationship; obligations persist after divorce

name: Father's Authority Over Daughter (Reshut HaAv)
notes: Father's legal rights over minor daughter: betrothal proceeds, earnings, found objects, vow nullification, receiving her get

name: Captive Woman's Purity (Ishto Shevuyah)
notes: Presumption of violation for women captured by enemy forces; husband obligated to redeem wife; priest's wife who was captured

name: Kohen's Daughter Ketubah (Four Hundred Zuz)
notes: Custom of priestly courts to grant four hundred dinars ketubah for a virgin daughter of a priest

name: Relocating a Wife (Havasat Ishah)
notes: Limits on husband's right to compel wife to move between towns or lands; three geographic regions of Israel

name: Compelling Aliyah to Eretz Yisrael in Marriage
notes: Either spouse may compel the other to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael or move to Jerusalem; refusal as grounds for divorce

name: Rape Fine (Kenas Oness)
notes: Fine paid to father of raped young woman; who qualifies, who is exempt; distinction from seduction; rapist must marry victim

name: Seduction Fine (Kenas Mefateh)
notes: Fine paid to father for seduction of a young woman; three vs. four payments compared to rape; seducer may release the woman

name: False Defamation Fine (Motzi Shem Ra — Ketubah Context)
notes: Husband falsely claims wife was not a virgin; 100 sela fine and prohibition from divorcing her; does not apply to converts

name: Husband Administering Oath to Wife
notes: Husband's right to administer oaths regarding wife's management of household property; ability to waive this right in ketubah

name: Husband Who Went Overseas (Ba'al sheHalakh leMedinah haYam)
notes: Wife's entitlement to sustenance when husband is overseas; oath requirements upon his return; third party who sustained the wife

name: Ketubah Currency and Geographic Variation
notes: Which currency standard applies when husband and wife married and divorced in different countries or regions

name: Distribution of Estate Among Orphans
notes: Rules for distributing estate when there are multiple creditors, widows, and heirs including the 'weakest one' dispute between R. Tarfon and R. Akiva

name: Mi'un (Refusal by Minor Girl)
notes: Minor orphan girl's right to refuse marriage arranged by mother or brothers upon reaching majority; no ketubah entitlement upon refusal

name: Rulings of Admon (Seven Decrees)
notes: Seven disputed rulings by the Jerusalem judge Admon, including field ownership after signing as witness, lost path to field, cross-debts

name: Rulings of Ḥanan ben Avishalom
notes: Two rulings by Jerusalem judge Ḥanan regarding wife's oath when husband is overseas and reimbursement to one who sustained another's wife

name: The Mouth That Prohibited is the Mouth That Permitted (Peh sheAsar hu Peh sheHitir)
notes: Credibility principle: one who admits a fact that creates a prohibition is believed when claiming it no longer applies; used extensively in Ketubot

name: Evidence of Virginity at Wedding (Edut al Betulah)
notes: Forms of testimony and evidence establishing that a woman was married as a virgin, including witnesses to hinnuma and distribution of roasted grain

name: Priest Forbidden to Remarry His Divorcée
notes: Practical halakhic consequence that a priest is given extra time before being forced to divorce, since he cannot remarry his ex-wife

name: Dowry for Orphan Girl from Charity
notes: Charity administrators' obligation to provide at least fifty dinars dowry for an orphan girl they marry off

name: Widow's Sale of Estate Property for Sustenance
notes: Rules governing a widow's right to sell her late husband's property to fund her sustenance; whether in court or outside court; limits on overselling

name: Sons vs. Daughters in Small Estate
notes: Dispute between Admon and Rabbis: when estate is insufficient for both sons' inheritance and daughters' sustenance, daughters take precedence

name: Yevama's Property Rights Pending Levirate Marriage
notes: Rights of a widow waiting for her yavam regarding property she inherits; how her usufruct property is treated before and after yibbum
